channel.title: HeavyMusix: metal news from around the world
channel.description: Metal news written by HeavyMusix: new albums, tours, festivals, the underground and Arizona metal.

item.title: Ex-Lamb of God drummer Chris Adler and Stone Sour bassist Johny Chow form new band Insidias, booked for Hellfest 2027
item.description: Chris Adler is back behind a full band. The former Lamb of God drummer has teamed up with Stone Sour bassist Johny Chow, French guitarist and songwriter Peter Scheithauer (ex-Temple of Brutality) and singer Jon Rioux of Defined in a new band called Insidias. The four came together and rehearsed in Nashville in October. Their debut album is being made now with producer and mixer Machine. There is no title or release date yet, and the band has no record label behind it. The first show is already set: Insidias will play Hellfest 2027 in Clisson, France, the festival's 20th-anniversary edition on June 17 to 20. Adler left Lamb of God in 2019, and Insidias is his biggest new band since then.

item.title: Mastodon book 28-date "Poisonous Weapons Tour" across Europe and the UK in spring 2027, with Monolord and Green Lung
item.description: Mastodon are taking "Marrow Deep", the album they released this summer, across Europe and the UK. "The Poisonous Weapons Tour" runs from March 14 at L'Olympia in Paris to April 23 at Große Freiheit 36 in Hamburg, with stops in Spain, Portugal, Germany, Scandinavia, Finland, Poland, Hungary, Austria and more. Monolord support on every date. Green Lung join for the four UK nights: Brixton Academy in London on March 30, Manchester on March 31, Glasgow on April 2 and Birmingham on April 3. The London show is Mastodon's first UK headline night since January 2019. This is the first full European headline run for the current lineup of Troy Sanders, Brann Dailor, Bill Kelliher, Nick Johnston and João Nogueira. General tickets go on sale today, November 27, at 10 a.m. local time.

item.title: Carcass announce "Europa Rigor Mortis Part III", a 20-date March 2027 European tour with Rotten Sound and BAT
item.description: Carcass are heading back across Europe in March 2027. "Europa Rigor Mortis Part III" packs 20 shows in 15 countries into just over three weeks, starting March 5 at Astra Kulturhaus in Berlin and ending March 27 at Gruenspan in Hamburg. The run takes the band through Poland, Czechia, Slovenia, Slovakia, Hungary, Bulgaria, Greece, Serbia, Croatia, Italy, Switzerland and Scandinavia, including a slot at Oslo's Inferno Metal Festival on March 25. Finnish grindcore band Rotten Sound support on every date, and BAT, the Richmond, Virginia speed-punk trio led by Ryan Waste of Municipal Waste, open the bill. Carcass are still touring behind "Torn Arteries", released in September 2021 on Nuclear Blast.

item.title: On this day in metal: Ozzy Osbourne's double live album "Talk of the Devil" climbs the UK chart (1982)
item.description: On November 27, 1982, Ozzy Osbourne's double live album "Talk of the Devil" was riding the UK albums chart, where it reached No. 21. In the United States and most other countries the same record was called "Speak of the Devil". Forty-four years on, it remains one of the best-known live records of Ozzy's early solo years.

item.title: Anthrax announce 19-date 2027 UK and European tour with Kerry King and Arizona's Sacred Reich
item.description: Anthrax will take the "Cursum Perficio Tour 2027" across the UK and Europe next spring, with Slayer's Kerry King and his solo band as direct support and Arizona's own Sacred Reich on every date. The run is 19 shows in 12 countries, opening March 14 at Dublin's 3Arena and closing April 10 at London's OVO Arena Wembley. Stops include Amsterdam, Paris's L'Olympia, Bilbao, Madrid, Barcelona, Milan, Zurich, Padova, Hamburg, Cologne, Berlin, Munich, Budapest, Prague and Brussels, plus Katowice's Spodek as part of Maniac Festival. More support acts will be announced in the coming months. The tour follows "Cursum Perficio", released earlier this year. Tickets go on sale Friday, November 27 at 10 a.m. local time, with limited VIP packages for every date. Back in the States, Anthrax and Kerry King play Phoenix with Megadeth on May 15.

item.title: Sweden's Entombed reunite for Sweden Rock Festival 2027 and work on their first album together since 1997
item.description: Swedish death metal pioneers Entombed will play Sweden Rock Festival in Sölvesborg, which runs June 9 to 12, 2027. The lineup is guitarists Alex Hellid and Uffe Cederlund with drummer Nicke Andersson, the trio behind "Left Hand Path" and "Wolverine Blues". The singer and the day of the show have not been announced yet. The three are also writing new music. The album in progress will be their first together since 1997; a title and release date are still to come. The show lands more than six years after the death of singer L-G Petrov, who died in March 2021 at 49.

item.title: The Black Dahlia Murder bring back guitarist Brandon Ellis as Wes Hauch departs
item.description: The Black Dahlia Murder have welcomed guitarist Brandon Ellis back into the band. He takes over from Wes Hauch, who leaves on good terms to give his full attention to his band Alluvial. Ellis first joined in 2016 and played on 2024's "Servitude", the band's latest album. He stepped away in February 2025 after nine years, and Hauch was named his replacement that May. The band's message to fans was short and hopeful: "We have a big year coming up." It starts this winter with the 20th anniversary "Nocturnal" run across Europe.

item.title: On this day in metal: Quiet Riot's "Metal Health" becomes the first heavy metal album to hit No. 1 (1983)
item.description: On November 26, 1983, Quiet Riot's "Metal Health" climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard 200, knocking The Police's "Synchronicity" off the top. It was the first heavy metal album ever to reach No. 1 on that chart. The album had been out since February 1983 on Pasha Records, produced by Spencer Proffer, and it took about nine months of steady climbing to get to the top.

item.title: Beyond Creation will play "The Aura" in full on a 2027 North American tour with Decrepit Birth and Vulvodynia, including Mesa on February 20
item.description: Montreal tech-death band Beyond Creation are marking 15 years of their debut album "The Aura" by playing it front to back across North America for the first time. Decrepit Birth and Vulvodynia are on every date of the run, which starts February 7 in Detroit and reaches Montreal on March 5, with more dates still to be announced. Arizona gets the 11th of the 22 announced shows: Saturday, February 20, 2027 at The Rosetta Room in Mesa, between West Hollywood and Albuquerque. Tickets go on sale Friday, November 27 at noon local time. The band will also play "Reverence", their first new song in eight years, every night. They are working on a fourth album, and a 15th-anniversary double vinyl reissue of "The Aura" is out now on Season of Mist.

item.title: Poland's Mgła surprise-release fifth album "Traitors to the Human Cause", their first in seven years
item.description: Kraków black metal duo Mgła dropped their fifth full-length, "Traitors to the Human Cause", on November 24 with no warning and no promo run, the way fans have come to expect from them. It is their first studio album since "Age of Excuse" in 2019. The record runs seven tracks and about 42 minutes, closing with the eight-minute title track. M handles guitars, bass and vocals and Darkside plays drums. It is out now digitally on the band's own No Solace label, with the CD shipping around December 7 and cassette and vinyl planned for 2027. Mgła are already booked for a run of 2027 European festivals, including Inferno in Oslo, Ragnarök in Germany, Brutal Assault in the Czech Republic and Party.San.

item.title: Paradise Lost celebrate 40 years with "The Final Ascension" European tour in November 2027, with Voivod and Dool
item.description: British doom-death pioneers Paradise Lost will mark their 40th year with "The Final Ascension", a November 2027 European tour that the band frames as closing a chapter. Canadian sci-fi thrash veterans Voivod and Dutch band Dool are the support. The run opens in Dublin on November 4 and takes in Glasgow, Lisbon, London, Paris, Tilburg, Düsseldorf, Brno, Dresden and Munich, with one date still to be announced. The set will draw on "Ascension", the band's 17th album, released in 2025. An artist presale opens today, November 25, at 10 a.m. GMT for the band's mailing list, and general sale starts Friday, November 27.

item.title: On this day in metal: Alice Cooper's "Poison" peaks at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 (1989)
item.description: On November 25, 1989, Alice Cooper's "Poison" reached its peak of No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, the high point of his late-'80s comeback and his last trip into the US top ten. The song was the lead single from his 18th album, "Trash", released by Epic in July 1989. Cooper wrote it with Desmond Child and John McCurry, and Child produced it.

item.title: Iron Maiden close their 2026 run in Yokohama tonight; one last North American leg comes in spring, with Phoenix on April 26
item.description: Iron Maiden play the first of two nights at K-Arena Yokohama in Japan today, November 24, with the second on November 25. They are the last shows of the 2026 stretch of the "Run For Your Lives" world tour, the 50th-anniversary run that started in Budapest in May 2025 and leans on the band's first nine albums, from the 1980 debut through "Fear of the Dark". The band first said they would rest through 2027, then changed course in October and added 16 North American shows they call the third and final leg. It opens April 14 at the Tacoma Dome and ends May 16 at Boardwalk Rock in Ocean City, Maryland, with a Sonic Temple headline slot in Columbus on May 14. Bullet For My Valentine and The Raven Age are the special guests on an all-British bill. Arizona gets its night on Sunday, April 26, 2027, at Talking Stick Resort Amphitheatre in Phoenix, between San Bernardino and Dallas. Steve Harris said the leg goes to places the band missed, especially the Northwest and Southeast. When it wraps, the tour will have played 107 shows to more than 3 million fans in 36 countries.

item.title: The Devil Wears Prada and 156/Silence join The Plot In You's 2027 tour, with Phoenix on March 23
item.description: The Plot In You have named the support for their spring 2027 headline run: The Devil Wears Prada as direct support, with 156/Silence opening the night. The bill was announced on November 23. The 26-date tour starts March 12 at The Factory in St. Louis and ends April 18 at The Pinnacle in Nashville, with stops in Denver, Los Angeles, Dallas, New York, Toronto and Chicago along the way. It follows "The Volumes Series", the set the band finished this summer on Fearless Records. Arizona's date is Tuesday, March 23, at Arizona Financial Theatre in Phoenix. It's on the HeavyMusix Arizona shows list at heavymusix.com/az.

item.title: Ryan McCombs leaves Drowning Pool for the second time to focus on SOIL
item.description: Singer Ryan McCombs is leaving Drowning Pool again. In a statement on November 23 he said the two sides will officially part ways as the band heads into 2027, and that the timing is right for everyone. McCombs first fronted Drowning Pool from 2005 to 2011 and came back in early 2023 after Jasen Moreno left. With him, the band released the singles "Revolution (The Final Amen)", "Madness" and "The Wrong One". No replacement has been named. He now turns his attention to SOIL, his other band, which signed with Better Noise Music, shared the single "Enemy X" in October and plans a new album for 2027.

item.title: On this day in metal: Metallica release the covers double album "Garage Inc." (1998)
item.description: On November 24, 1998, Metallica released "Garage Inc." on Elektra, a two-disc set made entirely of other people's songs. Disc one was mostly new recordings produced with Bob Rock: Discharge, Diamond Head, Black Sabbath, the Misfits, Mercyful Fate, Blue Öyster Cult, Nick Cave and more. Disc two gathered their earlier covers in one place, including the "Garage Days Re-Revisited" EP, "Am I Evil?", "Breadfan", "Stone Cold Crazy" and their Motörhead tribute tracks. It entered the Billboard 200 at No. 2 and went on to sell more than five million copies in the US. Their take on "Turn the Page" topped the mainstream rock chart, and "Whiskey in the Jar" won the Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance in 2000.

item.title: New metal releases this week: Mystic Prophecy, Leviathan, King 810 and Sacral Rage lead a packed November 27
item.description: Friday, November 27 brings a mixed and heavy pile of new records. German five-piece Mystic Prophecy return with "In Metal" on Perception, led by the single "Robots". The lineup is R.D. Liapakis on vocals, Dan Baune on guitar, Tommy Gun on bass and Christophe de Combe on drums. Leviathan drops "Die To This" through Profound Lore, while Flint, Michigan's King 810 self-release "La Grande Mort Or Silence Of God", produced by Josh Schroeder and previewed with "Love Kills". Heavy metal fans should also look for Sacral Rage's "Ark Of Cosmic Resonance" on No Remorse and Sarlic Bliss with "Melodies Of A Dying Dawn". Also out Friday: Devastator's "Goathammer" EP on Listenable, Revnoir's "Sometimes I Feel You, Sometimes I Don't" on Arising Empire, Neal Morse & The Resonance's "River Of Light", Molly Hatchet's "Lost Horizon" and the Saint Vitus tribute "Doom Shall Rise". On the reissue side, Pungent Stench's "Dirty Rhymes And Psychotronic Beats" and Vinterland's "Welcome My Last Chapter" return.

item.title: Forever Deaf Fest 2027 books Sanguisugabogg, Author & Punisher, Thou and Gutalax for Chicago in April
item.description: Chicago's Forever Deaf Fest has named its first 16 bands for 2027. The festival runs April 9 and 10 at Avondale Music Hall, with a pre-party on April 8 at Sleeping Village. The bill leans hard into the extreme end: Sanguisugabogg, Author & Punisher, Thou, Gutalax, Cephalic Carnage, Crippling Alcoholism, Scalp, Deadguy, Ancient Death, Anagnorisis, Chained To The Bottom Of The Ocean, Gylt, Intercourse, Barren Heir, Si Dios Quiere and Death Pose. Ticket details have not been announced yet.

item.title: Mongolia's The HU book 12 shows across Australia, New Zealand and Asia for March 2027
item.description: Mongolian band The HU will spend March 2027 in the Asia-Pacific region. The run has 12 dates from March 6 to 24. It opens March 6 in Auckland at Te Paepae Theatre, then hits Adelaide, two nights at Sydney's Enmore Theatre, two at Forum Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth. After that the band plays Megaport Festival in Kaohsiung City, Taiwan on March 20 and 21, then Tokyo's Yebisu Garden Hall on March 23 and Osaka's Club Quattro on March 24. Skáld open the Australian and New Zealand shows. There are no US dates on this run.

item.title: Norway's Slomosa bring the "Mute Tour" to the US in May 2027, with Welcome To Rockville and Sonic Temple
item.description: Norwegian band Slomosa have booked their "Mute Tour" across the US for spring 2027. The run has 11 dates between May 5 and May 20. Two big festival slots anchor the trip: Welcome To Rockville on May 8 and Sonic Temple on May 13. There is no Arizona date on this leg.

item.title: Slayer's Tom Araya and Kerry King host the metal station in Grand Theft Auto VI
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI has a metal radio station, and Slayer are running it. The game's station is called The Chamber 106.6, and its hosts are Kerry King and Tom Araya. Comedian Brian Posehn also turns up as "Big Fan Brian". The playlist reportedly includes Slayer's "Raining Blood", Metallica's "Battery" and "Master Of Puppets", Megadeth's "Symphony Of Destruction", Anthrax's "I Am The Law", Black Sabbath's "I", Pantera's "I'm Broken", Sepultura's "Territory", Overkill's "Rotten To The Core", Mastodon's "Blood And Thunder" and Tool's "Sober". Other reported picks include Dio's "We Rock", Exodus' "Bonded By Blood", Iron Maiden's "The Trooper", Judas Priest's "Freewheel Burning" and Flotsam & Jetsam's "Hammerhead". Full song lists are still being pieced together by players.

item.title: Impending Doom share "I Have Seen The Light" from "At The Throne Of God", their first album in almost eight years
item.description: Impending Doom are back with their first full-length in nearly eight years. The new album is called "At The Throne Of God" and has 12 tracks. The first single, "I Have Seen The Light", is out now. Orders are open through the band's own store, and the album reaches digital services on February 5, 2027.

item.title: Poland's Dopelord get a Season of Mist reissue of "Black Arts, Riff Worship & Weed Cult"
item.description: Polish doom band Dopelord, formed in 2010, are seeing their second album return. Season of Mist will reissue 2014's "Black Arts, Riff Worship & Weed Cult" on January 22, 2027. It comes on CD, black vinyl, and clear vinyl with purple splatter. Songs include "Addicted to Black Magick", "Preacher Electrik", "Acid Trippin'" and "Green Plague". The band recently finished a European tour with Monolord.

item.title: Arizona metal this week: As I Lay Dying in Tucson Tuesday, Psycroptic in Mesa on Friday, plus Nervosa and Currents booked for 2027
item.description: Two strong club shows hit Arizona this week. As I Lay Dying play 191 Toole in Tucson on Tuesday, November 24, at 7:30 PM. On Friday, November 27, Psycroptic headline The Rosetta Room in Mesa, with Inferi, Cognitive and Summoning The Lich on the bill. Metal Blade lists it as part of the band's North American headlining tour. New for 2027: Nervosa play The Rosetta Room in Mesa on February 2, Boundaries come to Mesa's Nile Theater on March 5, and Currents play the Marquee Theatre in Tempe on March 9. Every date is on our Arizona shows list, with directions and venue phone numbers.

item.title: On this day in metal: Black Sabbath release "The Eternal Idol" (1987)
item.description: On November 23, 1987, Black Sabbath released "The Eternal Idol" in the UK on Vertigo, their 13th studio album. It was the first Sabbath album with Tony Martin on vocals, alongside Tony Iommi, Bob Daisley on bass, Eric Singer on drums and Geoff Nicholls on keyboards. The US release followed on December 8 through Warner Bros. The record had a rough birth. Ray Gillen sang the first version of the songs and then left the band, so Martin joined in 1987 and recorded the vocals again. Several producers came and went before Chris Tsangarides finished the job. "The Shining" was the single and got a video. Other tracks include "Ancient Warrior", "Glory Ride" and "Born to Lose". The album reached No. 66 in the UK and No. 168 on the US Billboard 200.

item.title: Festival lineup roundup: Download 2027 books Bring Me The Horizon, Evanescence and blink-182, with Faith No More, Carcass and Napalm Death
item.description: Download Festival has revealed its first wave for 2027, and it is a big one. The UK festival returns to Donington Park from June 9 to 13, 2027 for its 24th edition, with Bring Me The Horizon, Evanescence and blink-182 sharing the top of the bill. It is blink-182's first time at Download, and Evanescence become the festival's second female-led headliner. More than 100 bands were announced in this first wave. For the heavier crowd, the bill already includes Faith No More, a special performance from Mötley Crüe, Static-X, Body Count featuring Ice-T, the reunited Murderdolls, I Prevail, Malevolence, Converge, Dayseeker, plus Carcass and Napalm Death. Tickets are on sale now. The organizers say the early bird tickets sold out in under two weeks, the fastest-selling Download ever, and that more bands and surprises are still to come.

item.title: 70000 Tons of Metal 2027 has 46 of its 60 bands booked, with Arch Enemy, Exodus and Forbidden on board
item.description: The world's biggest heavy metal cruise is taking shape. 70000 Tons of Metal sails January 14 to 18, 2027 on Royal Caribbean's Freedom of the Seas, leaving Miami for Puerto Plata in the Dominican Republic and returning to Miami four nights later. Forty-six of the planned 60 bands are already on the official lineup. Names on board include Arch Enemy, Exodus, Forbidden, Warbringer, Obscura, Exmortus, DGM, Vintersorg, Visions of Atlantis, Firtan, Thulcandra, Fires in the Distance, Avaland and Famous Strangers. Every band plays twice across four stages, including a pool deck stage, for more than 120 performances in all. Only about 3,000 tickets are sold for each sailing.

item.title: Arizona metal in March 2027: Haken and Nile with Coroner in Mesa, Clutch and Corrosion of Conformity at The Van Buren
item.description: March is shaping up to be a heavy month in the Valley. Prog metal band Haken bring their In A Fever Dream tour to the Nile Theater in Mesa on March 7, 2027, with Thank You Scientist and Leprous frontman Einar Solberg as support. Three nights later, on March 10, the same Mesa room hosts the Underworld Dissonance co-headline tour, with Nile and Coroner each playing a headline set, plus Syn Absence. Then on March 21, Clutch bring their Give The People What They Want tour to The Van Buren in Phoenix with Corrosion of Conformity, Agnostic Front and Chuck Ragan. Add Dying Fetus and Cryptopsy at Rebel Lounge and Firewind with Powerglove at the Rosetta Room, both on March 7, and Arizona's spring is already stacked.

item.title: Clutch announce 14th album "Wasted Lands" for January 22 and share "Beware The Fever"
item.description: Clutch will release their 14th studio album, "Wasted Lands", on January 22, 2027 through their own label, Weathermaker Music. The first single, "Beware The Fever", is out now. The band will tour hard behind it. A January run in Australia with Corrosion of Conformity comes first, then the 28-date Give The People What They Want tour of the US, from February 5 in Honolulu to April 4 in Brooklyn, with Corrosion of Conformity, Agnostic Front and Chuck Ragan on the headline dates. Arizona fans get their night on March 21 at The Van Buren in Phoenix.

item.title: Nile and Coroner team up for the 31-date "Underworld Dissonance" US tour in March and April
item.description: Two very different kinds of extreme metal share one stage next spring. Nile and Coroner will co-headline the Underworld Dissonance tour of the United States, 31 shows that run from March 2, 2027 in Greenville, South Carolina to April 11 in Leesburg, Virginia. Both bands play a full headline set each night. Nile are still touring "The Underworld Awaits Us All", released in August 2024 on Napalm Records, and Coroner are behind "Dissonance Theory", released in October 2025 on Century Media. Syn Absence open, with one more special guest still to be named. The tour stops at the Nile Theater in Mesa, Arizona on March 10.

item.title: The Black Dahlia Murder take "Nocturnal" across Europe for its 20th anniversary this winter
item.description: The Black Dahlia Murder are marking 20 years of "Nocturnal", their 2007 album on Metal Blade Records, with a European headline tour called Two Decades Of Nocturnal. The run is 29 shows in 13 countries, from January 14, 2027 at Batschkapp in Frankfurt to February 14 at Substage in Karlsruhe. Along the way the band hit Berlin, Copenhagen, Stockholm, Oslo, Prague, Krakow, Budapest, Vienna, Paris and London's The Dome, plus a slot at Drachten Deathfest in the Netherlands.

item.title: Metallica's All Within My Hands foundation gives $100,000 to help children affected by domestic violence in Las Vegas
item.description: Metallica's charity, the All Within My Hands Foundation, has given a $100,000 grant to SafeNest, Southern Nevada's largest nonprofit working to end domestic and sexual violence. The money pays for two years of staff and programs for the Child Advocacy and Support team at One Safe Place, SafeNest's new Family Justice Center, which opened in October. That includes weekly support sessions, a year-long program for children aged 7 to 17, and meals and resources for parents and caregivers. The foundation tied the gift to the fans who came to Las Vegas for Metallica's "Life Burns Faster" shows at Sphere.

item.title: On this day in metal: Sonata Arctica release their debut album "Ecliptica" (1999)
item.description: On November 22, 1999, Finnish power metal band Sonata Arctica released their first album, "Ecliptica". It was the start of the band's recording career. Spin it today and hear where it all began.

item.title: Band business tip: register every song so the royalties actually reach you
item.description: Releasing music is only half the job. If your songs are not registered in the right places, money from streams, radio and live plays can sit unclaimed. A royalty checklist published by Hypebot breaks it into a few simple layers, and every band can work through it in an afternoon. Songwriting first: join a performing rights organization where you live (ASCAP or BMI in the US, PRS in the UK, GEMA in Germany) and register each song with every writer and their split. If you publish yourself, sign up as both writer and publisher. In the US, also register with The MLC to collect streaming mechanicals. Then the recordings: SoundExchange in the US, PPL in the UK or GVL in Germany pay out for the master, and if you are both the band and the label, register as both. Keep the details identical everywhere. Each recording needs its own ISRC code and each song an ISWC, and the names and splits should match at your distributor, your PRO and The MLC. Claim your artist profiles on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube, check your credits about two weeks after every release, and look at unclaimed-royalty portals every few months. One more date for the calendar: the last Bandcamp Friday of 2026 is December 4, when Bandcamp waives its share of sales.

item.title: Firewind and Powerglove team up for the "Firepower USA Tour 2027", ending in Mesa on March 7
item.description: Greek power metal band Firewind are coming to the US with video-game metal crew Powerglove as co-headliners. The 11-date run starts February 23 in Austin and stops in Dallas, Kansas City, Iowa City, Chicago, Milwaukee, Denver, Salt Lake City, San Francisco and Los Angeles. Arizona gets the final night: Sunday, March 7, 2027 at the Rosetta Room in Mesa. The tour backs Firewind's new album "Gods, Myths & Titans", a Greek mythology concept record out February 19 on BLKIIBLK. Henning Basse is back on vocals, and the songs "Firegod" and "The Legend Of Achilles" are the first highlights.

item.title: Bloodstock 2027 adds Khemmis, Crisix, The Zenith Passage and 14 more; day tickets go on sale November 27
item.description: The UK's Bloodstock Open Air has added 17 bands to its 2027 festival, held August 5 to 8 at Catton Park in Derbyshire. Mercyful Fate, Electric Callboy and Motionless In White headline the main Ronnie James Dio Stage. New on the main stage are Pintglass on Friday and Brat and Pest Control on Sunday. The Sophie Lancaster Stage picks up Denver doom band Khemmis, Spanish thrashers Crisix, tech-death band The Zenith Passage, Viscera, Soldiers Of Rage, Only Pain, De Profundis, Devora, VCTMS, Redeemon, Muddibrooke, Endeavour, Pryma and The Five Hundred. Day tickets go on sale Friday, November 27, and the festival is offering a three-payment plan for the first time. Bloodstock is also premiering clips from Sepultura's last UK festival set on its YouTube channel on November 23, 25 and 27.

item.title: Judas Priest add Welcome to Rockville and seven European dates to their 2027 tour
item.description: Judas Priest keep growing their 2027 schedule. New shows include Welcome to Rockville in Daytona Beach, Florida on May 7, then Groningen in the Netherlands on June 22, Gothenburg on June 30, Uppsala on July 1, Riga on July 6, Gliwice in Poland on July 8, Burg Clam in Austria on July 10 and Istanbul on July 17. They join festival slots already on the books, including Boardwalk Rock in Ocean City, Maryland, Tons of Rock in Oslo, Copenhell, Tuska in Helsinki, Masters of Rock in Czechia and Release Festival in Athens. There is no Arizona date so far.

item.title: As I Lay Dying book a 16-date European tour for spring 2027
item.description: Metalcore band As I Lay Dying will tour Europe from April 20 to May 16, 2027. The run opens at Matrix in Bochum, Germany and heads through Leipzig, Ostrava, Vienna, Bucharest, Sofia, Athens, Thessaloniki, Belgrade, Zagreb, Venice, Milan and Paris before closing at De Helling in Utrecht. No support acts have been named yet. Tickets are on general sale now.

item.title: Gates To Hell unveil new singer JP Kaine on crushing single "Rotting Heart"
item.description: Louisville, Kentucky metallic hardcore band Gates To Hell have a new voice. The Nuclear Blast band parted ways with singer Ryan Storey and brought in JP Kaine, who also fronts Surfaced. "Rotting Heart" is the first song with him, and it comes with a video directed by Errick Easterday. The track was recorded, mixed and mastered this summer by Randy LeBoeuf in New Jersey. No album has been announced yet. The band are on the road supporting Guilt Trip from November 27 to December 16, and they are booked to support Avatar in June 2027.

item.title: U.D.O. share "The Sky Is The Limit" video from 20th album "Voodoo Ranger"
item.description: German heavy metal veterans U.D.O. have released a video for "The Sky Is The Limit", the second track on "Voodoo Ranger". The 12-song album, the band's 20th, arrives January 8, 2027 on Reigning Phoenix Music, following the earlier single "I'll Die Trying". Drummer Sven Dirkschneider says the song is about having the courage to follow your own path. The lineup is Udo Dirkschneider, Sven Dirkschneider, Fabian "Dee" Dammers, Peter Baltes and Alen Brentini. Udo also has an autobiography due the same month, and a "Triple Anniversary Tour 2027" across Europe marks 40 years of U.D.O. as a live band.
